transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, it's nice to meet you too. I came in because, well... people keep telling me they can't follow what I'm trying to explain. Like, I'll be writing my artist statements, or even just jotting down client notes, and my brain just starts jumping. I go from talking about the textures of the canvas directly into the budget for the exhibition, and then suddenly I'm explaining the secret meanings behind the colors... which reminds me, I actually ran out of cerulean blue yesterday. It's so frustrating because you can't just buy a good cerulean anywhere, you have to go to that one specific art supply store downtown, the one next to the bakery that makes those amazing almond croissants. I used to go there every Tuesday when I was in college for my bachelor's... but anyway, yeah, even in meetings, people just look at me like I'm speaking a different language.
Have you been feeling unusually high or overly energetic lately?

Well, yeah, sometimes I do. There are these stretches where I just feel completely lit up, you know? Like I'm almost unstoppable and every single idea I have is just brilliant. I'll be painting for hours and it's like the brush is an extension of my soul. But then, out of nowhere, a collaborator will make some tiny comment—like maybe they don't love the framing—and I just snap. Like, really snap, in a way that feels way bigger than the situation. It reminds me of this one time last year when I was working on a mural project with this guy, Dave. Dave was always so particular about the scaffolding, which, I mean, safety first, right? But he insisted on using these heavy steel pipes instead of the lighter aluminum ones, and it took us three extra days just to set up. I remember it rained the whole second day, just this miserable drizzle that made everything slick and dangerous. We had to huddle under a tarp eating these soggy sandwiches from a deli across the street... I think they were turkey and swiss? Anyway, yeah, I get really energized, but then I get so irritable if someone interrupts my flow.
Have you been hearing voices that other people don’t hear?

Well, yeah... I guess so. Sometimes when I'm alone in the studio, especially late at night, I'll hear this woman's voice. It's really quiet, like she's just whispering or commenting on things from right behind the storage shelves. And sometimes I'll smell this really strong scent of hot metal, usually when I'm standing near an unfinished piece. It feels so completely real, like she's right there, but then I'll walk around the shelves to check, and there's absolutely nothing. Just my boxes of old sketches and that one broken easel I can't bring myself to throw away. I bought that easel at a flea market in Brooklyn... oh, man, that flea market was amazing. They had these vendors selling vintage typewriters and old brass keys, and I bought this beautiful green glass bottle that I thought would look perfect on my windowsill. I carried it around the whole day in my tote bag, which was getting so heavy because I also bought a stack of old postcards from the 1920s. The handwriting on them was so loopy and elegant, you know? People don't write like that anymore. But yeah, the voice and the smell... they feel real until I look.
Have you ever heard that woman's voice during a time when you were not feeling especially energized or high?

Yeah, actually. There was this one month... maybe a couple months ago? I wasn't feeling all lit up or unstoppable at all. I was actually sleeping pretty normally, just kind of coasting, you know? But I still kept hearing her. Just those little comments from behind the shelves. And it wasn't just the voice, either. I started noticing these hidden warnings in my studio materials. Like, the way the bristles on my brushes were fraying, or the way the paint was separating in the tubes... it all felt like a message I was supposed to decode. Which reminds me, I really need to clean my brushes better. I've been using this cheap soap from the grocery store, the one with the lavender on the label. I thought it would be nice, you know, aromatherapy while I clean, but it leaves this weird residue on the bristles. My friend Sarah told me about this special brush conditioner she gets imported from France, but she's always exaggerating how good things are. Like this one time she convinced me to go to this pop-up vegan restaurant... oh my god, the line was two hours long, and it was raining again! I swear it's always raining when I try to do something nice. But yeah, the voice and the warnings... they were definitely there for a few weeks even when I wasn't feeling super energized.
Have you ever had a period where you felt deeply depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had days where I felt a bit down or uninspired, but nothing like a deep, dark depression every single day. Usually if I'm not feeling that high energy, I'm just kind of neutral. Like that coasting feeling I mentioned. It's actually kind of nice sometimes to just sit by the window and watch the street. I have this big bay window in my apartment, and I put all my plants there. I have this one monstera that is just going absolutely crazy. It's putting out these massive leaves with all the holes in them—fenestrations, I think they're called? I spent like three hours watching this YouTube video about how to properly stake them with a moss pole, but the guy in the video had the most annoying voice. He sounded exactly like my high school geometry teacher, Mr. Henderson, who used to make us do these ridiculous proofs on the chalkboard while he drank coffee that smelled like burnt tires. I hated geometry. I always wanted to be in the art room instead. But yeah, no long stretches of being super depressed, just normal days.
Have you ever had a period of feeling unusually high or energized that lasted at least a week?

Yeah, definitely. Sometimes I get these stretches where I just feel completely lit up, you know? Like I'm practically vibrating with energy and I'm totally unstoppable. Every single idea I have feels absolutely brilliant, and I'll just be sketching and painting for days. But then... I don't know, my friend or someone I'm working with will make just one tiny comment about a piece, and I'll just snap. Like, completely blow up at them over nothing. It's way bigger than the situation actually calls for. I did that to my friend Mark last week when he said he didn't like the shade of blue I was using. Which is ridiculous because Mark doesn't even know anything about color theory! He wears these awful plaid shirts with striped ties, I swear it gives me a headache just looking at him. I tried to tell him once that he should look into getting his colors done—you know, like finding out if he's an autumn or a winter? I think he's a winter, honestly, but he insists on wearing these mustard yellows that wash him out so bad. I saw this TikTok where this girl draped different colored fabrics over people to find their season, and it was so satisfying to watch. I ended up buying a bunch of fabric scraps from a craft store to try it on myself, but the cashier was so rude! She practically threw my change at me. I hate when people don't have basic customer service skills. But yeah, those high energy periods definitely happen, and I can get pretty irritable during them.
When you were not feeling especially high or energized, did the voice and those warnings continue for at least a month?

Yeah, like I was mentioning earlier, it was a solid month. I had that quieter month where I was sleeping totally normally and not feeling unstoppable or anything, but I still kept hearing her comments from behind the shelves and reading those hidden warnings into my ordinary studio materials for several weeks. 

Speaking of those shelves, I actually really need to reinforce them. I bought them from IKEA, and you know how that goes. I spent an entire Saturday trying to put the main bookcase together, and the little Allen wrench they give you is just... it's practically a joke. I ended up dropping one of the main structural screws, and it rolled all the way under my refrigerator. Have you ever tried to move a refrigerator by yourself? It's completely impossible. I had to use a broom handle to fish the screw out, and I ended up pulling out all these little fuzzy mouse cat toys instead, which is super weird because I don't even own a cat. The girl who lived in my apartment before me must have had one. I think her name was Jessica? She still gets mail delivered here sometimes, mostly these massive catalogs for outdoor camping gear. I don't understand who needs to look at that many fleece jackets, honestly. It takes up so much room in the mailbox. 

But yeah, the voice and the warnings definitely kept going for at least a month while my energy was just totally normal.
